steps.name: What it covers
steps.meaning: The parts that have a curve, their share of the value, and what has none yet
steps.fact: 1 part with a curve · 4 without one yet
paragraphs: Hail on solar farms: logistic curves per module type fitted to public PVEL/Kiwa hail-test breakage anchors and the IEC baseline; glass-breakage probability used as the module replacement ratio. It names 1 part: PV modules (glass and cells). Outside its scope: yearly and tail loss metrics (computed by the consumer, not the cell) and site value and exposure basis (supplied by the consumer). Kinds of damage it does not include: cell cracking or latent performance loss without glass breakage and wind-driven hail hitting the module face (open seam, not in the diameter-only curve).

For this hazard the solar farm is split into 1 part: PV modules (glass and cells). Parts of the plant's value with no curve yet: racking structure (secondary, open; no curve), tracker steel (used only as a stow conditioner; direct damage has no curve), SCADA and met instruments (optional secondary; no curve) and inverters, substation, foundations, civil works and drainage (treated as no direct hail damage by coverage decision; no curve).

The damage ratio is a share of replacement value of the PV modules; the plant share comes from a named value profile (direct module hardware, or the Hazard-compatible adapter) or a site value basis, with no default. The files state no plant-level dollar figure for this asset. Shares of the plant's physical value, as the cell states them: PV modules (glass and cells) 33 %.

assumptions.text: Primary operational x-axis is maximum hail diameter / MESH-equivalent size, not kinetic energy.
assumptions.trigger: Provider supplies reliable KE-native or KE-flux hazard layer.
assumptions.effect: Changing to KE-native would require hazard data conversion for most providers.

assumptions.text: v1 treats glass breakage probability as module replacement damage ratio.
assumptions.trigger: Claims/repair policy data or module-specific post-hail replacement criteria.
assumptions.effect: If broken modules are not always replaced, DR would be too high; if non-broken cell cracks lead to replacement, DR could be too low.

assumptions.text: IEC 25mm pass is represented as near-zero module replacement probability: 1.0% default, 0.5% hardened.
assumptions.trigger: Better field data for 25–35mm replacement damage.
assumptions.effect: A different near-zero anchor moves D50/k slightly.

assumptions.text: Default module archetype is 3.2mm glass//backsheet when exact specs are absent.
assumptions.trigger: Exact module BOM / datasheet / hail test certificate.
assumptions.effect: If actual modules are thin glass//glass, default underestimates damage; if hardened, overestimates.

assumptions.text: Hardened curve tail beyond public anchors is extrapolated.
assumptions.trigger: Expanded hail test results for hardened designs across 50–76mm.
assumptions.effect: Extreme-hail losses for hardened modules may be over/underestimated.

assumptions.text: Stowed state shifts selected D50 by +8mm.
assumptions.trigger: Tracker-specific hail stow testing or validated angle-to-energy model.
assumptions.effect: Controls benefit of stow around transition zone; material effect on 45–65mm losses.

assumptions.trigger: Empirical stow loss reduction / exposed-area study.
assumptions.effect: Affects high-end loss cap under stowed state.

assumptions.text: If stow state is unknown, expected DR is a probability-weighted blend of stowed and unstowed states.
assumptions.trigger: SCADA logs, command confirmation, alert lead-time records.
assumptions.effect: If probability is wrong, expected DR is wrong; deterministic states avoid this.

assumptions.text: Default exposure_fraction is 1.0 until site swath overlay is available.
assumptions.trigger: GIS overlay of MESH swath and array footprint.
assumptions.effect: May overstate loss for localized swaths; appropriate for conservative full-footprint scenario.

assumptions.text: Non-module subsystems are reviewed and treated as DR≈0/secondary for direct hail in v1.
assumptions.trigger: Claims/source evidence for distinct material direct-hail equipment loss.
assumptions.effect: If evidence shows material direct hail damage to trackers/enclosures/instruments, add a curve.

assumptions.text: f_hail material share is a placeholder value-link parameter inside PV_ARRAY.
assumptions.trigger: Module BOM / replacement cost allocation specific to module glass/cell failure.
assumptions.effect: Controls cap_L; changes asset-level loss cap materially.

open_seams.name: Module BOM / glass-cell at-risk f
open_seams.description: Hail cap depends on what share of PV_ARRAY value is actually exposed module glass/cell value.
open_seams.resolution: Dedicated module BOM sourcing pass; placeholder until sourced.

open_seams.name: Hail diameter-to-impact-energy bridge
open_seams.description: Operational data are diameter/MESH, but module physics and lab anchors may be impact-energy-native; bridge assumptions can affect curve position.
open_seams.resolution: Create versioned bridge assumptions from diameter to mass/velocity/KE; keep provider axis diameter-native.

open_seams.name: Tracker stow is hazard-correlated conditioner
open_seams.description: Actual stow angle depends on forecast, lead time, controls, and operator execution.
open_seams.resolution: Represent as conditioner in v1; future stochastic P(stowed | forecast) if needed.

open_seams.name: Does hail materially damage trackers/racking?
open_seams.description: Tracker/racking may be more a conditioner than a damaged failure-unit.
open_seams.resolution: Source damage cases or set DR≈0 with notes.

open_seams.name: Glass thickness and module construction unknown
open_seams.description: Substrate has hazard-linked module specs but public data not fully populated.
open_seams.resolution: Use manufacturer/site data when available; generic placeholder otherwise.

open_seams.name: Site MESH exceedance frequency
open_seams.description: EAL and return-period loss require a site-specific MESH frequency curve.
open_seams.resolution: Source from hazard provider, MRMS/MESH frequency analysis, insurer map, or site study.

open_seams.name: P(stowed | forecast/control/lead time)
open_seams.description: Stow is currently scenario-weighted, not a stochastic operations model.

open_seams.name: Footprint exposure fraction
open_seams.description: Site loss depends on how much of the asset footprint is inside the damaging hail swath.
open_seams.resolution: Use event footprint overlay / MESH raster intersection.

open_seams.name: Extreme tail beyond final threshold
open_seams.description: PML/tail metrics require a credible tail distribution and curve spread.
open_seams.resolution: Use provider exceedance tail or EVT/statistical fit.
